PRINCIPLE: Memory should work like human associative thinking. You type a word ('cocaine', 'YouTube', 'ADHD') and the system semantically retrieves relevant one-liners about that concept from Ned's history, injects them before the model answers. If a headline looks especially relevant, the model can call expand to get full context.

SOURCE: Ned's direct articulation — 'I just want memories, proper memories. So when I actually talk about things, it brings shit up.' The frustration is re-introducing himself every session.

APPLICATION: The retrieval mechanism already exists in rlabs (7 activation signals, expand endpoint). The failure was in WHAT got stored (duplicates, surface-level). Fix the input (curation quality) and the retrieval works.

NOT THIS: Cross-project code knowledge graphs, architecture maps, 'what API endpoint does X call'. That's a different product. This is about the person, not the code.

NOT THIS EITHER: One global CLAUDE.md file. Too static, goes stale, not associative.

THE BAR: 'When I ask about YouTube, it knows I started YouTube. When I ask about ADHD, it surfaces what I said about it in October. Without me re-explaining.'
